description:
Harlet Pack 3D Files USB Overview

The Harlet Pack 3D Files USB contains STL and STEP files for the three most popular designs in the Harlet family: the Harlot, the Longshot, and the Brawler. All three are single-shot, break-action .22LR derringers built on the same proven platform. Each design offers a different take on the compact pistol concept, from the original pocket-sized Harlot to the extended-barrel Longshot to the distinctive knuckle duster Brawler.

These are beginner-friendly builds. If you can operate a 3D printer and turn a screwdriver, you can complete any of these pistols. The files are organized and ready to slice. Plug in the USB and start printing.

What’s on the USB

Harlot [1.0]
The original. A compact single-shot .22LR derringer designed from the ground up for accessibility. The Harlot is one of the most user-friendly 3D printed firearms available. Simple break-action design, minimal parts, and straightforward assembly. Uses a 1″ rifled barrel liner. This is where most builders start with the Harlet platform.

Longshot
The extended-barrel variant. Same proven Harlot fire control group stretched to a 3″ barrel for improved accuracy and velocity. Eight barrel configurations included: iron sights, Picatinny rail options, and optic cuts for RMR, Glock MOS, C-More, Docter, and Shield red dots. If you want precision from the Harlet platform, this is the design to print.

Brawler
The statement piece. The Brawler wraps the Harlot platform in a knuckle duster grip that’s equal parts functional firearm and conversation starter. Uses a 2″ barrel with the same fire control group as other Harlet variants. Also includes the BrassTax files if you want to machine a metal-framed version.

Why the Harlet Pack

Three Designs, One Platform
All three pistols share the same fire control group, breech design, and general assembly process. Learn one, and you understand them all. The skills transfer directly between builds, making this pack ideal for builders who want variety without starting from scratch each time.

Beginner-Friendly Builds
The Harlet family was designed for accessibility. No press-fitting, no complex machining, no specialized tools beyond what comes in the hardware kits we sell. These are ideal first projects for builders new to 3D printed firearms.

Offline Access
Once you have the USB, you have the files permanently. No reliance on websites staying online or download links staying active. Your files, your drive, always available when you need them.

Organized and Ready
Files are sorted by design and clearly labeled. No hunting through folders or figuring out which version is current. Plug in and start slicing.

What You Still Need

Hardware Kits
Each design requires a hardware kit containing the barrel liner, springs, and fasteners. We sell kits for all three designs: Harlot Build Kit, Longshot Build Kit, and Brawler Build Kit. The USB contains files only.

3D Printer and Filament
Any standard FDM printer with a typical build volume will work. PLA+ is the recommended material. The Harlet designs were created to print on entry-level machines without specialized modifications.

Basic Tools
Hex drivers, wire cutters, epoxy, and a soldering iron for heat-set inserts on optic-cut barrel options. Nothing exotic.

Harlet Pack USB FAQ

What file formats are included?
The USB contains STL and STEP files ready for slicing. STL files work with any slicer. STEP files are included if you want to modify the designs.
Are hardware kits included?
No. This USB contains print files only. Hardware kits (barrel liners, springs, fasteners) are sold separately. We offer kits for all three designs in the pack.
What printer do I need?
Any standard FDM printer with a typical build volume will work. The Harlet designs were created for entry-level machines. No specialized modifications required.
What filament should I use?
PLA+ is the tested and recommended material for all three designs. Nylon and polycarbonate have also been used successfully by experienced builders.
Which design should I build first?
Start with the Harlot. It’s the simplest of the three and will teach you the platform. Once you’ve completed one Harlot, the Longshot and Brawler are easy to understand since they share the same fire control group.
Is building these designs legal?
Under federal law, individuals may manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. State and local laws vary significantly. Some jurisdictions prohibit home-built firearms entirely. Verify your local laws before printing.
What about the metal weight requirement?
Federal law requires handguns to contain a minimum of 3.7oz of metal. UFA-compliant grip spacers are included in the file packages for installing the required weight. Metal is not included in this USB or the hardware kits.

USB Contents

Designs Included: 3 (Harlot, Longshot, Brawler)

Caliber: .22 LR

Action: Single-shot, break-action

File Formats: STL, STEP

Barrel Options: 1″ (Harlot), 2″ (Brawler), 3″ (Longshot)

Recommended Filament: PLA+

Not Included: Hardware kits, filament, metal weight

description:
AR15 Lower Parts Kit Overview

The AR15 Lower Parts Kit includes everything you need to complete a stripped lower receiver. This is a full mil-spec LPK with quality components throughout, not a bag of mystery parts from overseas. The trigger group is mil-spec, the springs are black oxide coated for corrosion resistance, and every piece is made in the USA.

One thing that sets this kit apart is the included billet trigger guard. Most lower parts kits ship with a stamped aluminum guard that requires a roll pin and careful installation to avoid cracking your lower. The billet guard in this kit is stronger, looks better, and installs easier. It’s a small upgrade that makes a real difference during assembly.

What’s Included in This AR15 LPK

Fire Control Group
Mil-spec hammer, trigger, and disconnector with all associated springs and pins. The trigger and hammer have polished sear surfaces for a clean break. Standard mil-spec pull weight around 6-7 lbs. These parts are investment cast, not MIM, so you don’t have to worry about a cheap hammer breaking on you.

Safety Selector
Standard 90-degree throw selector with detent and spring. Crisp, positive engagement in both safe and fire positions.

Bolt Catch Assembly
Bolt catch, plunger, spring, and roll pin. Proper engagement with the bolt carrier and magazine follower for reliable last-round hold-open.

Magazine Release
Magazine catch, button, and spring. Standard AR15 pattern compatible with all mil-spec magazines.

Pivot and Takedown Pins
Both pins with their detents and springs. These connect your upper and lower receivers and allow field stripping.

Buffer Retainer
Buffer retainer and spring. Keeps the buffer in place when you separate the upper and lower.

Billet Trigger Guard
Machined aluminum trigger guard, not stamped. Stronger than standard guards and easier to install. No roll pin required on most designs.

A2 Pistol Grip
Standard A2 grip with screw and lock washer. The classic grip that works. Swap it out later if you want something different, but this gets you shooting.

Black Oxide Springs
All springs in this kit are black oxide coated. This finish resists corrosion better than bare steel and looks cleaner than the shiny springs in cheaper kits.

What You Still Need

Stripped Lower Receiver
This kit completes a stripped lower. You need the receiver itself, whether that’s a standard forged lower, billet lower, or 80% build you’ve finished yourself.

Buffer Tube Assembly
The LPK does not include the buffer tube, buffer, buffer spring, castle nut, or end plate. You’ll need a complete buffer kit or stock assembly to finish the lower.

Stock or Brace
For a rifle build, you need a stock. For a pistol build, a brace or bare buffer tube. This depends on your barrel length and intended configuration.

AR15 Lower Parts Kit FAQ

Is this a complete lower parts kit?
Yes. This kit includes every part needed to assemble a stripped lower receiver except the buffer tube assembly (buffer, spring, tube, castle nut, end plate) and stock. The trigger guard, pistol grip, fire control group, and all small parts are included.
Will this work with any AR15 lower?
This kit fits any mil-spec AR15 lower receiver chambered in 5.56/.223, or other standard AR15 calibers. It also works with 80% lowers and 3D printed receivers designed for mil-spec parts.
What’s the trigger pull weight?
The mil-spec trigger group has a pull weight around 6-7 lbs. It’s a standard military-style trigger with some creep before the break. If you want a lighter or crisper trigger, you can always drop in an aftermarket trigger later.
Can I upgrade to a drop-in trigger?
Yes. Install this kit first, then swap the hammer, trigger, and disconnector for a drop-in trigger cassette. You’ll still use the safety selector, pins, and other components from this kit.
What tools do I need for installation?
A punch set, hammer, and pivot pin installation tool make the job easier. You’ll also want a lower receiver vise block if you have one. Most people complete the install with basic hand tools in under an hour.
Is the trigger guard enhanced or standard?
This kit includes a billet aluminum trigger guard, which is an upgrade over the standard stamped guards in most kits. It’s stronger, easier to install, and looks better.
Are the parts made in the USA?
Yes. Every component in this kit is manufactured in the United States.

Specifications

Platform: AR15/M4

Caliber Compatibility: 5.56/.223

Trigger Group: Mil-spec

Trigger Guard: Billet aluminum

Pistol Grip: A2 style

Springs: Black oxide coated

Made in: USA

Not Included: Lower receiver, buffer tube assembly, stock

description:
AR15 Magpul M3 30rd Mag Overview

The Magpul PMAG M3 is the gold standard for AR15 magazines. This is a 30-round polymer magazine for 5.56 NATO and .223 Remington that’s been tested and proven across military, law enforcement, and civilian use worldwide. When people talk about reliable AR magazines, they’re usually talking about PMAGs.

The Gen M3 version incorporates upgraded materials and manufacturing processes that exceed military performance specifications. The constant-curve internal geometry feeds smoothly, the anti-tilt follower prevents jams, and the stainless steel spring holds up through thousands of cycles. Magpul makes these in the USA with a reputation they’ve built over two decades of making gear that works.

What Makes the PMAG M3 Different

Anti-Tilt Follower
The four-way anti-tilt follower ensures the top round stays in position as the spring pushes it up. This eliminates the feeding issues that plague cheaper magazines where the follower can rock or tilt under spring pressure.

Constant-Curve Geometry
The internal curve of the magazine body is engineered for smooth feeding throughout the full 30-round stack. No hang-ups at the top, middle, or bottom. The design has been refined through millions of rounds of real-world testing.

Impact and Crush Resistant
The polymer construction handles drops, impacts, and pressure that would crack or deform lesser magazines. Magpul tests these in extreme heat, cold, mud, sand, and general abuse. They keep working.

Over-Insertion Stop
A stop on the spine prevents the magazine from being inserted too far, which can cause feeding issues on some platforms. The magazine seats positively and consistently every time.

Tool-Free Disassembly
The floorplate pops off without tools for easy cleaning and spring inspection. Reassembly is just as simple. No special equipment needed to maintain your magazines.

Paint Pen Matrix
The dot matrix on the bottom panel lets you mark magazines for identification. Useful when you want to track specific loads or identify magazines during training.

Compatibility

The PMAG M3 is optimized for Colt-spec AR15/M4 platforms, which covers the vast majority of AR15 rifles on the market. The Gen M3 design also works with non-Colt-spec platforms including the HK 416, MR556A1, M27 IAR, British SA-80, and FN SCAR MK 16/16S.

For builders, the PMAG M3 works with standard AR15 lowers, 80% builds, and 3D printed AR15 receivers designed for mil-spec magazines. If your lower takes standard AR magazines, this fits.

Magpul PMAG M3 FAQ

What’s the difference between M2 and M3 PMAGs?
The M3 has improved geometry for wider platform compatibility (HK 416, SCAR, etc.), an over-insertion stop, aggressive texturing, the paint pen matrix, and enhanced materials. The M2 works fine in standard AR15s, but the M3 is the more refined design.
Can I leave these loaded long-term?
Yes. Magpul designs these magazines to be stored loaded without spring fatigue or feed lip deformation. The polymer is creep-resistant, meaning it won’t spread over time like some materials.
Does this come with a dust cover?
Yes. The PMAG M3 includes a pop-off impact/dust cover that protects the feed lips during storage and transport. The cover is optional for use but included in the package.
Will this work in my AR pistol or SBR?
Yes. Barrel length doesn’t affect magazine compatibility. If your AR pistol or SBR uses a standard mil-spec lower, PMAG M3s work perfectly.
Can I use Ranger Plates with the M3?
Yes. The M3 floorplate is compatible with Magpul Ranger Plates for enhanced handling, or you can swap to a slim-line floorplate for tighter pouch compatibility.
Is this magazine reliable enough for duty use?
The PMAG M3 is used by military and law enforcement units worldwide. It’s proven reliable in combat conditions across multiple continents. For duty, defensive, or hard use, this is a go-to magazine.
What states restrict this magazine?
Several states prohibit magazines over 10 or 15 rounds. Restricted states include California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois (some areas), Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, Oregon, and Washington DC. Check your local laws before ordering.

Specifications

Caliber: 5.56×45 NATO / .223 Remington

Capacity: 30 rounds

Material: Impact and crush resistant polymer

Follower: Four-way anti-tilt, self-lubricating

Spring: Stainless steel, USGI-spec

Compatibility: AR15/M4, HK 416, M27 IAR, FN SCAR MK 16, SA-80

Features: Over-insertion stop, dust cover included, tool-free disassembly

Color: Black

Made in: USA

description:
G19/17 50rd Drum Mag Overview

The 50rd Drum Mag holds 50 rounds of 9mm in a compact drum configuration that fits all double-stack Glock pistols. Load it up, lock it in, and you have serious capacity for range days, competition stages, or home defense setups. The drum feeds reliably and drops free when empty.

The body is glass-filled polymer with hardened steel reinforcement where it matters. Inside, a heat-treated chrome silicon wire spring handles the tension needed to push 50 rounds through the feed system. A ratcheting load assist lever makes loading manageable since stuffing 50 rounds by hand would get tedious fast.

Why Choose a 50-Round Drum

Maximum Capacity, Minimum Reloads
Fifty rounds is nearly three times what a standard G17 magazine holds. For range sessions where you want to shoot more and reload less, or competition stages where round count matters, the drum keeps you in the fight longer.

Works Beyond Pistols
This drum fits any platform that accepts Glock double-stack 9mm magazines. That includes pistol caliber carbines like the Kel-Tec Sub 2000, AR9 builds, and other Glock-mag compatible PCCs. The extra capacity makes even more sense in a carbine where you’re shooting faster and want fewer mag changes.

Load Assist Lever
The ratcheting load assist lets you wind in rounds without destroying your thumbs. Essential when you’re loading 50 rounds at a time. The mechanism is built into the drum body for easy access.

Steel-Reinforced Construction
The polymer body is glass-filled for impact resistance, with steel inserts at critical stress points. The combination keeps weight manageable while maintaining durability where the magazine takes the most abuse.

Compatibility

This drum magazine fits all double-stack 9mm Glocks from Gen 1 through Gen 5. That includes the Glock 17, 17L, 18, 19, 19X, 26, 34, 45, and 47. It also works in 3D printed frames built for double-stack Glock magazines, such as the DD17.2, DD19.2, and DD26.2.

The drum is also compatible with most pistol caliber carbines that accept Glock magazines. Function in PCCs is generally reliable, though the manufacturer notes that fit and function in carbines is not guaranteed since there are many different PCC designs on the market.

Not compatible with single-stack Glocks like the G43, G43X, or G48.

50rd Glock Drum Magazine FAQ

Does this drop free when empty?
Due to the weight of the loaded magazine, it may not drop free as quickly as a standard stick magazine. When empty, it should release and drop normally. Some shooters strip it out manually during reloads just to be sure.
Can I use this with hollow point ammo?
The manufacturer recommends using FMJ ammunition. Hollow points may not feed as reliably due to the drum’s feeding geometry. Test thoroughly with your carry ammo if you plan to use this for defensive purposes.
Will this work in my AR9?
If your AR9 or PCC uses Glock magazines, this drum should fit. Many shooters run these in AR9 builds and Kel-Tec Sub 2000s successfully. Some PCCs may have tighter magwells, so function isn’t guaranteed across all platforms.
How hard is it to load?
The ratcheting load assist lever makes loading much easier than it would be otherwise. You wind in rounds using the lever rather than fighting spring pressure with your thumb. It still takes a few minutes to load 50 rounds, but it’s not painful.
Can I disassemble this for cleaning?
The manufacturer advises against disassembly. Opening the drum voids the warranty. For cleaning, you can flush the exterior and magwell interface without taking it apart.
Will this work with 3D printed Glock frames?
Yes. If your printed frame accepts standard double-stack Glock magazines (DD17.2, DD19.2, DD26.2, G80, Geisler Defence, etc.), this drum will work. It’s a popular choice for builds where maximum capacity is the goal.
What states restrict this magazine?
Several states prohibit magazines over 10 or 15 rounds. Restricted states include California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois (some areas), Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, Oregon, and Washington DC. Check your local laws before ordering.

Specifications

Caliber: 9mm Luger

Capacity: 50 rounds

Configuration: Drum

Body Material: Glass-filled polymer with steel inserts

Spring: Heat-treated chrome silicon wire

Weight: 1.5 lbs (empty)

Compatibility: Glock 17, 17L, 18, 19, 19X, 26, 34, 45, 47 (Gen 1-5)

Features: Load assist lever, polymer follower

Warranty: Limited lifetime

short_description: Clear Extended Glock Magazine by ETS
description:
ETS 27rd Extended Glock Mag Overview

The ETS 27rd Extended Glock Mag gives you 10 extra rounds over a standard G17 magazine in a package that’s competition legal at 170mm. The clear polymer body lets you see exactly how many rounds you have left and what type of ammo is loaded. No more guessing or counting shots.

Elite Tactical Systems builds these magazines from an advanced polymer that handles abuse better than most. Drop it from 8 feet onto concrete and it won’t crack. Leave it loaded for months and the feed lips won’t spread. Run it in extreme heat, cold, or around harsh chemicals and it keeps working. ETS backs every magazine with a lifetime warranty and makes them in the USA.

Why Shooters Choose ETS Extended Magazines

See Your Round Count
The translucent clear body isn’t just for looks. You can glance at the magazine and immediately know how many rounds are left. During a stage, during training, or just doing a press check before you holster, you always know what you’re working with.

Competition Legal 170mm
USPSA and other competition organizations have rules about magazine length. At 170mm, this ETS mag meets the requirements for most divisions while still giving you 27 rounds of 9mm. More rounds, fewer reloads, better stage times.

Works with Your Existing Gear
The ETS magazine is compatible with both factory Glock floorplates and aftermarket basepads. If you already run extensions on your other mags, they’ll work here too. The ergonomic floorplate design also makes these easy to grab from a mag pouch under pressure.

Built to Last
The advanced polymer construction resists impacts, temperature extremes, UV exposure, and harsh chemicals. Unlike some aftermarket magazines that become brittle over time, ETS mags hold up in real-world conditions. The anti-tilt follower ensures reliable feeding through the full 27-round stack.

Compatibility

This magazine fits all double-stack 9mm Glocks from Gen 1 through Gen 5. That includes the Glock 17, 18, 19, 19X, 26, 34, and 45. It will also work in 3D printed frames designed for these platforms, including the DD17.2, DD19.2, DD26.2, and their remixes.

Not compatible with single-stack Glocks like the G43, G43X, or G48. Those use a different magazine pattern entirely.

ETS 27rd Glock Magazine FAQ

Will this work in my Glock 19?
Yes. The ETS 27rd magazine works in any double-stack 9mm Glock, including the G19. The magazine will extend below the grip since it’s longer than a standard G19 mag, but it functions perfectly.
Is this reliable for carry or just range use?
ETS magazines are reliable enough for carry. The polymer construction is extremely durable, and the anti-tilt follower ensures consistent feeding. Many shooters run ETS mags for both competition and everyday carry. That said, test any magazine thoroughly with your carry ammo before depending on it.
How does this compare to OEM Glock magazines?
The main advantages over OEM are higher capacity (27 vs 17 rounds), the translucent body for visual round count, and lower cost. ETS mags are well-made and reliable, though some shooters still prefer OEM for duty use. For range, competition, or home defense, ETS magazines perform well.
Will this work with 3D printed Glock frames?
Yes. If your printed frame is designed for double-stack Glock magazines (DD17.2, DD19.2, DD26.2, G80, Geisler Defence, etc.), this magazine will work. It’s a popular choice for builds where you want extended capacity.
Can I use my existing Glock mag extensions?
Yes. ETS magazines are compatible with factory Glock floorplates and most aftermarket basepads. The baseplate is also designed for easy disassembly if you need to clean or service the magazine.
Is the clear polymer durable?
Very. ETS rates these for 8-foot drops onto hard surfaces without cracking. The polymer also resists UV degradation, temperature extremes, and chemical exposure. The feed lips are creep-resistant, so they won’t spread even when stored loaded long-term.
What states restrict this magazine?
Several states have magazine capacity restrictions that prohibit 27-round magazines. These include California, Colorado, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois (some areas), Massachusetts, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, and Washington DC. Check your local laws before ordering.

Specifications

Capacity: 27 rounds

Length: 170mm (competition legal)

Material: Clear UV-resistant polymer

Follower: Anti-tilt

Compatibility: Glock 17, 18, 19, 19X, 26, 34, 45 (Gen 1-5)

Floorplate: Compatible with Glock and aftermarket basepads

Warranty: Lifetime

Made in: USA

description:
FGC9 MK2 Build Kit Overview

The FGC9 MK2 Build Kit gives you the hardware needed to build the most recognized 3D printed firearm in the world. The FGC9 MK2 is a 9mm pistol caliber carbine that can be built entirely from 3D printed parts and commonly available materials. This kit includes the precision components that are hardest to source: the prefabricated bolt, firing pin, rifled barrel, and all the metric hardware.

The FGC-9 (which stands for “F*** Gun Control, 9mm”) was developed as a proof of concept that functional firearms can be manufactured outside traditional supply chains. The MK2 version refined the original design with improved reliability, easier assembly, and better ergonomics. It uses a closed-bolt straight blowback action, feeds from either 3D printed magazines or OEM Glock mags, and has been successfully built and tested by thousands of people worldwide.

What’s Included in the FGC9 MK2 Kit

Prefabricated Bolt Assembly
The bolt is the most critical metal component in the FGC9. This kit includes a prefabricated bolt machined from 4140 steel rod, saving you the work of cutting, welding, and heat treating your own. Also includes the firing pin machined from 3mm steel rod. These parts are ready to install.

4.5″ Rifled Barrel
A rifled 9mm barrel with proper chamber dimensions. The original FGC9 design called for ECM rifling a hydraulic tube, which works but requires significant setup and experimentation. This barrel is ready to go out of the box.

Springs
All the springs you need for the build: buffer spring (0.93″ OD, 10.5″ length), hammer spring (17mm OD, 90mm length), and smaller springs for the trigger group and other assemblies. Getting the right spring rates is critical for reliable cycling, and these are spec’d to the FGC9 MK2 requirements.

Shaft Collars
DIN 705 shaft collars in 3mm (1x) and 16mm (3x). These retain the barrel and other components in the receiver.

Metric Hardware
Complete fastener set including M3, M4, and M6 socket head screws in various lengths, hex head screws, cup point set screws, nuts, washers, and external tooth washers. All DIN standard hardware as specified in the FGC9 documentation.

Steel Rod Stock
18mm 4140 steel rod (216mm and 50mm pieces) for bolt construction if you want to build additional bolts or need backup material. Also includes 3mm low carbon steel rod (100mm) for firing pin stock.

Brass Heat-Set Inserts
Four brass threaded inserts that get melted into the printed parts with a soldering iron. These provide durable metal threads in the polymer.

5mm Hex Key
The charging handle uses a 5mm Allen key as its core. This one is sized correctly at 82.5mm overall length with a 25mm short leg.

What You Still Need for Your FGC9 MK2 Build

Printed Parts (You Print These)
The FGC9 MK2 files are available from DEFCAD,. You’ll print the upper receiver, lower receiver, pistol grip, stock assembly, charging handle components, fire control group parts, and magazine components. PLA+ at 100% infill for critical parts. The file package includes detailed print settings.

Adhesives
JB Weld or similar steel-reinforced epoxy for bonding metal to printed parts. Loctite threadlocker for fasteners. Silicone spray for lubrication.

Magnets
20x10x2mm neodymium magnets for the magazine catch system. These are common and easy to source online.

Tools
Power drill, angle grinder with cutting discs, Dremel or rotary tool, metal files, soldering iron for heat-set inserts, digital calipers, vise, and metric bit drivers. The documentation lists everything in detail.

Magazine
You can print FGC9 magazines (25 rounds) using the included files, or use OEM Glock 17 magazines with the Glock magwell adapter (33 rounds with extended mags). Both options work reliably.

Why the FGC9 MK2

The Most Documented 3D Printed Firearm
No other design has been built, tested, and refined by as many people as the FGC9. The documentation is extensive, covering everything from print settings to assembly sequences to troubleshooting. If you run into a problem, someone has already solved it and posted the fix.

Practical Performance
This isn’t a novelty or a range toy. The FGC9 MK2 is a functional 9mm carbine that runs reliably when built correctly. Closed-bolt operation means better accuracy than open-bolt designs. The carbine length gives you a stable platform with a proper stock and enough barrel for decent velocity.

Skip the Hardest Steps
The original FGC9 build requires fabricating your own bolt and rifling your own barrel. Both are achievable but require significant time, tools, and trial runs. This kit gives you a prefabricated bolt and finished barrel so you can focus on the assembly rather than metalworking.

FGC9 MK2 Build Kit FAQ

What skill level is required for this build?
The FGC9 MK2 is an intermediate to advanced build. You should be comfortable with 3D printing, basic metalworking (grinding, drilling, filing), and following detailed technical documentation. This kit removes the most difficult steps (bolt fabrication and barrel rifling), but assembly still requires patience and attention to detail. Plan for 2-4 days of work spread across printing and assembly.
Is this a complete FGC9 kit?
This kit includes the hardest-to-source components: prefabricated bolt, firing pin, rifled barrel, all springs, all metric hardware, shaft collars, steel rod stock, brass inserts, and hex key. You provide the printed parts, adhesives, magnets, and tools.
Where do I get FGC9 MK2 print files?
DEFCAD hosts the complete FGC9 MK2 file package. The download includes STL files for all printed components, detailed assembly instructions, print settings, and a complete bill of materials.
Can I use Glock magazines?
Yes. The FGC9 MK2 works with both printed magazines (25 rounds) and OEM Glock 17/18 magazines using a printed magwell adapter. Glock 33-round extended mags give you maximum capacity. The Glock mag option is popular because the magazines are widely available and proven reliable.
What’s the difference between the FGC9 and FGC9 MK2?
The MK2 is the refined second version. Key improvements include a simpler bolt design, improved fire control group, better stock ergonomics, and easier assembly overall. The MK2 is more reliable and easier to build than the original. Always build the MK2 unless you have a specific reason to use the older design.
Do I still need to do any metalworking?
Some grinding and filing will be required to fit parts, but the heavy metalworking is done. The bolt and barrel in this kit are finished. You won’t need to weld, heat treat, or perform ECM rifling. Basic hand tools and a Dremel handle the remaining work.
Is building an FGC9 legal?
Federal law allows individuals to manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. State and local laws vary significantly. Some states restrict or prohibit home-built firearms, and some restrict features like detachable magazines or overall length. Verify your local laws before ordering.
What filament should I use?
PLA+ is the standard recommendation. Print at 100% infill for stress-bearing parts like the lower receiver and FCG components. description:
Magpul MOE Carbine Stock Overview

The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock (Mil-Spec) is a drop-in replacement buttstock for AR15/M16 carbines using Mil-Spec sized receiver extension tubes. Designed under Magpul’s Original Equipment line, the MOE Carbine Stock delivers a high-quality alternative to standard AR furniture at an economical price point without sacrificing the engineering and material quality Magpul is known for. Whether you’re upgrading a factory rifle or building from scratch, this is a straightforward, no-nonsense stock that gets the job done.

The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock features a streamlined A-frame profile optimized for light, fast action. This design minimizes snagging during shouldering and movement while shielding the release latch from accidental activation. A premium chrome-silicon lock spring ensures positive locking at each position and resists spring relaxation over extended use. The included 0.30″ rubber butt-pad provides anti-slip purchase against the shoulder, performing reliably even with body armor or modular gear. Made in the USA with NSN numbers assigned for government procurement.

The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock works with Mil-Spec sized carbine receiver extension tubes from manufacturers including Colt, LMT, Ruger, S&W, SIG, and Armalite. It weighs just 8.0 oz (12.0 oz with receiver extension), offers a 3.3″ length of pull adjustment range, and extends from approximately 10.5″ to 13.8″ LOP on a standard M4 receiver extension. Available in Black, OD Green, Flat Dark Earth, and Gray from the factory, with additional Cerakote options through select retailers.

What Makes the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock Different

Streamlined A-Frame Profile
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock utilizes a sleek A-frame design that reduces bulk and prevents snagging during dynamic movement or when transitioning between targets. This profile complements the natural lines of the AR platform while keeping the overall package compact and maneuverable.

Shielded Release Latch
The position adjustment lever is protected by the stock body, preventing accidental collapse during use. This addresses a common complaint with standard M4 stocks where the latch can be inadvertently pressed during shouldering or while wearing gear. The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock keeps the latch accessible but protected.

Premium Chrome-Silicon Lock Spring
Unlike standard carbine stocks that use conventional springs, the MOE Carbine Stock employs a chrome-silicon lock spring. This material provides stronger positive locking and resists relaxation over thousands of cycles, preventing the auto-collapse failures that can occur with lower-quality springs.

Sloping Cheek Weld
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock combines a slim profile with user comfort through its contoured cheek weld area. The design maintains a low profile while still providing consistent cheek placement for proper sight alignment. Compatible with Magpul CTR Cheek Risers for shooters who need additional height.

Multiple Sling Attachment Options
The stock includes integrated 1.25″ sling loops at the rear and bottom, plus a lanyard hole at the toe for custom paracord configurations. The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock is also compatible with Magpul ASAP, ASAP QD, and other receiver-mount sling attachments, giving you flexibility in how you configure your rifle.

Magpul MOE Carbine Stock FAQ

What is the difference between Mil-Spec and Commercial-Spec for the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock?
The critical difference is buffer tube diameter. Mil-Spec tubes measure approximately 1.148″ in diameter while Commercial-Spec tubes measure approximately 1.168″. The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock Mil-Spec model will only fit properly on Mil-Spec buffer tubes. A Mil-Spec stock will not fit on a Commercial tube (too tight), and a Commercial stock will be loose and wobbly on a Mil-Spec tube. If you are unsure which you have, measure your buffer tube with calipers or purchase the Mil-Spec version, as this has become the industry standard.
What manufacturers make compatible buffer tubes for the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock?
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock (Mil-Spec) is compatible with Mil-Spec sized carbine receiver extension tubes from Colt, LMT, Ruger, S&W, SIG, Armalite, and most other manufacturers producing Mil-Spec components. Most modern AR15 builds and factory rifles use Mil-Spec tubes. The receiver extension tube is not included with the stock.
What are the dimensions and weight of the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock?
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock weighs 8.0 oz on its own (12.0 oz when combined with a receiver extension). Maximum length is 6.9 inches. The length of pull adjustment range is 3.3 inches, providing approximately 10.5″ LOP when collapsed and 13.8″ LOP when fully extended on a standard M4 carbine receiver extension. Specifications may vary slightly depending on buffer tube manufacturer.
Is the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock compatible with cheek risers?
Yes. The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock features side mounting slots that accept Magpul CTR Cheek Risers. These risers are useful when the stock is fully extended or on rifles without rear-facing charging handles. The mounting slots also work for non-AR15/M16 applications where the stock is adapted to other platforms.
What sling mounting options does the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock offer?
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock provides multiple sling attachment points: integrated 1.25″ sling loops at the rear and bottom of the stock, plus a lanyard hole at the toe for custom paracord rigging. It is also compatible with Magpul ASAP, ASAP QD, and other receiver-mount sling attachments that mount to the lower receiver.
Is the rubber butt-pad on the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock removable?
Yes. The 0.30″ thick rubber butt-pad included with the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock is removable. This allows for replacement or cleaning. The pad provides an anti-slip surface and impact protection during shoulder transitions, performing effectively even when used with body armor or tactical gear.
What colors are available for the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock?
Factory colors from Magpul include Black, OD Green, Flat Dark Earth (FDE), and Gray. Some retailers offer additional Cerakote finishes including Pink, Tungsten, Titanium, Red, and Burnt Bronze. Cerakoted versions may show wear marks with heavy use as the coating is applied over the polymer body.
Does the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock have any play or wobble when installed?
The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock may have minimal play when installed, as it does not include the friction lock mechanism found on the more expensive Magpul CTR stock. For most users, the amount of movement is negligible and does not affect function. If eliminating all wobble is a priority, consider upgrading to the CTR model.

Compatibility

The Magpul MOE Carbine Stock (Mil-Spec) fits AR15, M16, M4, AR10, M110, and SR25 platforms equipped with Mil-Spec sized carbine receiver extension tubes. Compatible with buffer tubes from Colt, LMT, Ruger, S&W, SIG, Armalite, and other manufacturers producing Mil-Spec components.

Not Compatible

This Mil-Spec model will NOT fit Commercial-Spec buffer tubes (1.168″ diameter). Do not attempt to install on Commercial-Spec extensions. If you have a Commercial-Spec buffer tube, order the Magpul MOE Carbine Stock Commercial-Spec (MAG401) instead. Not compatible with rifle-length or pistol buffer tubes.

Legal Notice

This is a buttstock only and is not a firearm or regulated component. No FFL required for purchase. Magpul, MOE, CTR, ASAP, and related trademarks are the property of Magpul Industries Corporation. This product is manufactured by Magpul Industries. Made in the USA.

FGC-9 Mag Catch Overview

The FGC-9 Mag Catch is a machined aluminum replacement for the 3D-printed magazine catch on your FGC-9 MKII. While the printed mag catch works fine initially, it’s one of the weakest points in the design: thin, under constant spring pressure, and prone to warping or breaking over time (especially in hot climates).

This FGC-9 Mag Catch is machined from 6061 aluminum and finished with Mil-Spec MIL-A-8625 Type II black anodize. It’s a direct drop-in replacement for the printed part. No modifications, no fitting. Remove the old one, install this one, and never worry about your mag catch failing again.

Compatible with the FGC-9 MKII.

Why Upgrade to the Aluminum FGC-9 Mag Catch

Eliminate a Known Failure Point
The printed mag catch is thin, under spring pressure, and flexes every time you insert or release a magazine. Over hundreds of cycles, the plastic fatigues. In warm environments (garages, vehicles, outdoor use), PLA and even PLA+ can deform at temperatures well below what you’d expect. The aluminum FGC-9 Mag Catch doesn’t flex, doesn’t creep, and doesn’t care about the weather.

Mil-Spec Anodized Finish
MIL-A-8625 Type II anodize isn’t marketing fluff. It’s the same specification used on military small arms components. The finish provides corrosion resistance, wear resistance, and a consistent black appearance that won’t rub off or discolor over time.

Direct Drop-In Replacement
The FGC-9 Mag Catch is machined to the exact dimensions of the original printed part. Remove your old mag catch, install this one using the existing spring and pivot pin, and you’re done. No drilling, no filing, no modifications to your lower.

6061 Aluminum Construction
6061 is the standard for machined firearm components: strong, lightweight, and corrosion-resistant. The FGC-9 Mag Catch adds minimal weight while dramatically increasing durability compared to printed alternatives.

FGC-9 Mag Catch FAQ

Is the FGC-9 Mag Catch compatible with the original FGC-9 MKI?
This FGC-9 Mag Catch is designed specifically for the FGC-9 MKII. The MKI and MKII have different lower receiver designs. Verify your build version before ordering.

The printed mag catch is thin and under constant spring pressure. Over time, the plastic creeps and deforms. In hot environments (100°F+), PLA-based filaments soften significantly, accelerating failure. The aluminum FGC-9 Mag Catch eliminates these issues entirely.
What is MIL-A-8625 Type II anodize?
MIL-A-8625 Type II is the military specification for sulfuric acid anodizing of aluminum. It creates a hard, corrosion-resistant oxide layer that’s more durable than paint or other coatings. The black color is dyed into the anodized layer, not applied on top, so it won’t chip or peel.
Is this a regulated firearm part?
No. The FGC-9 Mag Catch is an unregulated component. It is not a firearm, frame, receiver, or controlled part. Ships directly to your door with no FFL required.

Modularity. A Polymer80 frame is a single integrated unit with serialized components, rails, and grip in one piece. Mac n Cheese [2.5] Build Kit Overview

The Mac n Cheese [2.5] Build Kit delivers everything you need to build a complete 3D printed M11-pattern pistol caliber carbine. This isn’t a hardware-only kit—it includes a complete 9mm side-cocking MAC-11 upper, AR15 fire control group with safety, stainless steel LRBHO components, and all the hardware required to finish your build. Print the lower, open the box, assemble.

The Mac n Cheese is a printable ambidextrous M11 lower receiver that introduced the first-ever Last Round Bolt Hold Open (LRBHO) system to the M11 platform. Version 2.5 brings significant improvements including a completely redesigned magazine catch, no-feedramp geometry, and an adjustable overtravel stop. Compatible with standard full-size 9mm M11 uppers, the Mac n Cheese accepts Glock magazines and uses a familiar AR15 fire control group.

What Makes the Mac n Cheese [2.5] Different

Integrated LRBHO – A Platform First
The Mac n Cheese pioneered Last Round Bolt Hold Open functionality on the M11 platform. When the magazine runs dry, the bolt locks back automatically—no more guessing whether you’re empty. The stainless steel LRBHO components included in this kit are precision-made for reliable function.

Completely Redesigned Magazine Catch
V2.5 addresses one of the biggest complaints about V2: the magazine catch now actually works. This isn’t a minor tweak—it’s a complete redesign that ensures positive magazine retention and reliable release. Combined with Glock magazine compatibility, reloads are fast and familiar.

No-Feedramp Design
Based on input from PY2A, Version 2.5 eliminates the feedramp entirely. This streamlined approach improves reliability while simplifying the printed geometry. The result is cleaner prints and more consistent feeding.

Ambidextrous Controls
The Mac n Cheese lower is fully ambidextrous from the factory. Left-handed shooters get the same experience as right-handed shooters without modifications or compromises.

AR15 Fire Control Group
Instead of proprietary trigger components, the Mac n Cheese uses a standard AR15 FCG with safety selector. Parts are common, affordable, and well-understood. The included FCG comes ready to install with the safety already fitted.

Adjustable Overtravel Stop
Fine-tune your trigger feel with the integrated adjustable overtravel stop. Dial in a crisp, short reset for faster follow-up shots and improved precision.

Core Components
Complete 9mm side-cocking MAC-11 upper with bolt and threaded barrel, stainless steel LRBHO assembly, AR15 fire control group with safety selector, and AR15 grip with grip screw. These are the functional components that turn your printed lower into a working firearm.

Assembly Hardware
5/16 clevis pin, M3x30 screw, M3x20 screw, three M4 grub screws, M4x35 screw, M4x45 screw, M5x70 screw, two M4 nuts, and one M5 nut. Everything required for complete assembly.

Mac n Cheese [2.5] Build Kit FAQ

Is the Mac n Cheese [2.5] Build Kit a complete firearm?
No. The kit includes the M11 upper, fire control group, LRBHO, grip, and hardware—but you must 3D print the lower receiver using the included files. The printed lower is the serialized component and firearm under federal law.
What magazines does the Mac n Cheese accept?
The Mac n Cheese lower is designed to accept Glock 9mm magazines. Standard Glock 17 magazines work, as do extended magazines and aftermarket Glock-pattern magazines from manufacturers like Magpul, ETS, and others.
What printer do I need to build the Mac n Cheese?
Any FDM printer with sufficient build volume will work. The design has optimized print orientations for reliable results. Prior experience with 3D printing is essential—your printer and materials must be properly calibrated to avoid issues with critical geometry. This is an intermediate to advanced build.
What filament should I use?
PLA+ is commonly used for 3D printed firearms. Higher-performance materials like glass-filled nylon or Zytel produce stronger results. Check the included documentation for specific recommendations and print settings.
Can I use my V2 bolt catch with the V2.5 lower?
Yes, with modification. The catch section needs to be trimmed for compatibility. A jig for this modification is in development. New builds should use the V2.5 bolt catch geometry.
What is the skill level required?
Intermediate to advanced. Prior experience with both 3D printing and firearm assembly is essential. Expect 1-2 days of build time depending on print speed and your familiarity with the assembly process.
Who designed the Mac n Cheese?
The Mac n Cheese was designed by MiddletonMade. V2.5 incorporates improvements and input from PY2A and the broader community. Files can be found at DEFCAD.

Under federal law, individuals may manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. However, state and local laws vary significantly. The forging process compresses the aluminum grain structure, creating superior directional strength compared to billet or cast alternatives. 7075-T6 offers higher tensile strength and hardness than 6061-T6, making it the preferred choice for hard-use builds.

Type III Hard Coat Anodized Finish
Type III anodizing (also called hard coat or MIL-A-8625 Type III) creates an extremely hard, wear-resistant oxide layer on the aluminum surface. This is the same finish specification used on military small arms. The black color is dyed into the anodized layer, not painted on top, so it won’t chip, peel, or rub off. Your finished lower will match other hard coat anodized AR components.

Safe/Fire Engravings Included
Selector markings are already engraved on the receiver: SAFE and FIRE in the standard positions. No need to add your own markings after machining. Install your safety selector and you’re ready to go.

Machined to military specification tolerances, this 80% lower accepts all standard AR-15 components. Any mil-spec lower parts kit, buffer assembly, pistol grip, trigger, and upper receiver will fit without modification. Once you complete the fire control pocket and pin holes, your lower functions exactly like a factory mil-spec receiver.

Yes, machining will expose raw aluminum in the fire control pocket, but for most builders this internal area is acceptable to leave uncoated or touch up with cold blue or aluminum black. What is the AR15 Anodized Lower Receiver [80%]?
An 80% lower is an unfinished receiver blank. Because it cannot accept a fire control group in this state, the ATF does not classify it as a firearm. You complete the final machining at home to create a functional stripped lower receiver.
Will machining damage the anodized finish?
Machining will remove the anodized finish inside the fire control pocket and around the drilled pin holes. However, these areas are internal and not visible once the lower parts kit is installed. The exterior finish remains intact. Most builders leave the machined areas as-is or apply a light coat of oil, cold blue, or aluminum black for corrosion protection.
What’s the difference between 7075-T6 and 6061-T6 aluminum?
7075-T6 is stronger and harder than 6061-T6, with higher tensile strength and better resistance to stress. It’s the mil-spec standard for forged AR-15 receivers and is used in military M16/M4 lowers. 6061-T6 is commonly used for billet receivers and is still plenty strong, but 7075-T6 is preferred for forged mil-spec builds.
What tools do I need to finish the AR15 Anodized Lower Receiver [80%]?
You’ll need an 80% lower jig (sold separately), a router or drill press, and appropriate end mills and drill bits. Some jigs are designed for handheld routers, others for drill presses or milling machines. Follow the jig manufacturer’s instructions for specific tooling requirements.

You can build rifles or pistols chambered in 5.56 NATO, .223 Remington, .223 Wylde, .300 Blackout, 6.5 Grendel, .458 SOCOM, and other AR-15 compatible calibers. The lower itself is caliber-agnostic: the upper determines what you’re shooting.
Is the AR15 Anodized Lower Receiver [80%] legal?

Others require serialization of all home-built firearms. It is your responsibility to verify the laws in your state before ordering. We do not ship to restricted states.

Federal law does not require serialization of firearms manufactured for personal use. However, several states (including California) require home-built firearms to be serialized. Always verify your state and local laws. If you intend to sell or transfer the firearm, additional federal requirements apply.
What parts do I need to complete my build after finishing the lower?
After machining, you’ll need: a lower parts kit (LPK) including trigger, hammer, safety, grip, and springs; a buffer tube assembly (buffer, spring, tube, and stock or brace); and an upper receiver assembly (upper, barrel, handguard, BCG, and charging handle). Complete upper assemblies are available that bolt directly onto your finished lower.

description:
3D Printed G43X Build Kit Overview

The 3D Printed G43X Build Kit gives you everything needed to complete your DD43.2 frame in one package. No more sourcing slimline parts from four different vendors and hoping they all work together. This kit includes the complete slide, frame parts, locking block, and precision rails, all matched for the DD43.2 platform.

The Glock 43X sits in a sweet spot for concealed carry. You get the slim single-stack profile of the G43 with a longer grip that holds 10+1 rounds instead of 6+1. For 3D printed pistol builders, the DD43.2 frame lets you build that same capability at home. Print your frame, install these components, and you have a functional slimline 9mm.

What’s Included in This 3D Printed Glock 43X Kit

Complete Glock 43X Slide
Full slide assembly ready for your build. The 43X slide shares dimensions with the G48 but pairs with the shorter G43 barrel. Includes all internals and sights. Compatible with standard G43/43X holsters and aftermarket accessories.

FMDA DD43.2 Rail
Precision-formed stainless steel rails built for the DD43.2 mounting system. The slimline Glock platform requires tighter tolerances than the double-stack frames, and these rails are manufactured specifically for that fitment. No-screw rear rail system for easier assembly and better frame durability.

Glock 43X Locking Block
CNC machined from 17-4 stainless steel. The locking block is critical for safe operation, keeping the barrel locked during firing and controlling unlock timing. This block is made to OEM specifications for the G43X platform.

Glock 43X Frame Parts Kit
Complete lower parts for your slimline build: trigger assembly, trigger housing with ejector, connector, all springs, slide stop, slide lock, pins, and magazine catch. These parts are specific to the 43X/48 platform and won’t interchange with double-stack Glocks.

Why Build a 3D Printed Glock 43X

Best Capacity in a Slim Package
The G43X frame holds 10 rounds flush-fit in a grip that’s still narrow enough for comfortable all-day carry. That’s the same capacity as many compact double-stacks in a package that disappears under a t-shirt. With Shield Arms magazines, you can push it to 15+1 in the same footprint.

One Kit, No Compatibility Guesswork
Slimline Glock parts aren’t as common as G19 components, so finding compatible pieces can be frustrating. We matched everything in this kit to work together on the DD43.2 frame. The slide fits the rails, the lower parts match the trigger housing, and the locking block is the correct spec. You’re building, not troubleshooting.

Proven Frame Design
The DD43.2 frame was developed by the FMDA community specifically for the slimline platform. It uses the improved DDxx.2 rear rail system that’s been refined across thousands of builds. The documentation and community support for this design are solid.

What Else You Need for Your 3D Printed G43X

DD43.2 Frame (You Print This)
Files are available free from DEFCAD, Odyssee, and The Gatalog. Search for “DD43.2” or look for CTX43x and similar remixes compatible with DD43.2 rails. PLA+ is the standard recommendation. The slimline frame requires more print precision than double-stack models, so follow the included settings closely.

Magazine
OEM Glock 43X magazines work perfectly. For higher capacity, Shield Arms S15 magazines fit the G43X/48 platform and hold 15 rounds in the same footprint. Note that Shield mags require a metal magazine catch, which is not included.

Basic Tools
Punch set, hammer, and a bit of patience. The slimline platform can be more finicky to assemble than a G19, but plenty of video tutorials cover the process.

3D Printed G43X Build Kit FAQ

Is this a complete 3D printed Glock 43X kit?
This kit includes all the metal and internal components needed to complete a DD43.2 3D printed frame. You provide the printed frame (free files available online) and a magazine. Everything else is in the box.
What’s the difference between the G43, G43X, and G48?
The G43 is the original single-stack with a short grip holding 6+1 rounds. The G43X has an extended grip for 10+1 while keeping the short G43 slide length. The G48 pairs that same longer grip with a longer G48 slide. The DD43.2 frame uses 43X dimensions with the extended grip.
Will G43 parts work with this kit?
Some parts interchange between the G43 and G43X, but not all. The lower parts kit, locking block, and rails in this kit are specific to the 43X platform. Don’t try to mix and match parts between different slimline models without verifying compatibility.
Where do I get DD43.2 print files?
DEFCAD, Odyssee, and The Gatalog host the files for free. Look for DD43.2 or compatible remixes like CTX43x. Print settings and assembly instructions are included in the download.
Is this harder to build than a G19?
Slimline builds can be more demanding. Tighter tolerances mean less room for error in printing and assembly. If this is your first 3D printed Glock, a DD19.2 might be an easier starting point. If you’re comfortable with the process, the DD43.2 is very achievable.
Is building a 3D printed ghost gun legal?
Federal law allows individuals to manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. State and local laws vary, and some places restrict or prohibit home-built firearms. Check your local laws before you order.
Can I use Shield Arms S15 magazines?
Yes, but you’ll need a metal magazine catch designed for the S15. The standard polymer mag catch can wear prematurely with metal magazines. Shield sells compatible catches separately.
Is the slide assembled?
The slide ships complete with all internals and sights installed. Unlike our G17 and G19 kits, this one is ready to drop onto your completed frame.

Kit Specifications

Platform: Glock 43X (slimline)

Capacity: 10+1 (OEM), 15+1 (Shield S15)

Rails: Stainless steel, DD43.2 pattern

Locking Block: 17-4 SS, G43X spec

Frame Compatibility: DD43.2 and compatible remixes

Not Included: Printed frame, magazine

description:
3D Printed G26 Build Kit Overview

The 3D Printed G26 Build Kit includes everything you need to finish your DD26.2 frame. The G26 is the subcompact version of Glock’s double-stack 9mm line, and finding matched parts for 3D printed builds can take some digging. This kit bundles the complete slide, frame parts, locking block, and precision rails into one purchase, all verified to work with the DD26.2 platform.

The Glock 26 has been a popular concealed carry choice since 1994. It holds 10+1 rounds in a frame short enough to disappear in an IWB holster, and it accepts any double-stack Glock magazine if you need more capacity. For 3D printed pistol builders, the DD26.2 frame brings that same versatility to the home shop.

What’s Included in This 3D Printed Glock 26 Kit

Complete Glock 26 Slide
Full slide assembly with barrel, internals, and sights. The G26 uses a shorter slide than the G19 but shares the same width, so holster and accessory options are plentiful. Compatible with Gen 3 Glock 26 pattern frames including the DD26.2.

FMDA DD26.2 Rail
Precision-formed stainless steel rails designed specifically for the DD26.2 frame. The front rails are a new design unique to this platform, not scaled-down versions of the G19 rails. The rear rails use the improved DDxx.2 no-screw mounting system that’s stronger and easier to assemble than earlier designs.

Glock 26 Locking Block
CNC machined from 17-4 stainless steel to Gen 3 Glock 26 specifications. The three-pin design fits the DD26.2 and its remixes. Quality matters here since the locking block takes significant stress during cycling.

Glock 26 Frame Parts Kit
Complete lower parts: trigger bar, trigger housing with 9mm ejector, connector, all springs, slide stop, slide lock, pins, and magazine catch. These drop into a properly printed DD26.2 frame without hand fitting.

Why Build a 3D Printed Glock 26

The Double-Stack Subcompact
The G26 holds 10+1 rounds in a frame that’s significantly shorter than a G19. For deep concealment, that extra half inch matters. And because it takes standard Glock double-stack magazines, you can run G17 or G19 mags with grip extensions when capacity is the priority.

One Kit, No Parts Hunt
G26-specific components aren’t as common as G19 parts. The locking block, rails, and frame parts are different from the larger models, and mixing parts between platforms causes problems. We put this kit together so everything matches and works on the DD26.2 out of the box.

DDxx.2 System Reliability
The DD26.2 uses the same improved rear rail design as the DD17.2 and DD19.2. FMDA developed this system to solve the assembly headaches and durability issues of earlier frames. The front rails were designed fresh for the G26 platform, not adapted from larger designs.

Also Compatible with .40 S&W
The DD26.2 frame accepts both G26 (9mm) and G27 (.40 S&W) slides. This kit ships with a 9mm upper. If you want .40, the rails and lower parts kit work for either caliber, so you can always add a G27 slide later.

What Else You Need for Your 3D Printed G26

DD26.2 Frame (You Print This)
Files are available free from DEFCAD, Odyssee, and The Gatalog. Search for “DD26.2” or “FMDA Glock 26.” The download includes print settings and assembly instructions. PLA+ works well for most builders. The subcompact frame prints faster than a G19 due to smaller size.

Magazine
Any Glock 26 magazine from Gen 3 through Gen 5, or aftermarket equivalents like Magpul PMAGs. G17 and G19 magazines also work and give you 17 or 15 rounds with the grip extension below the frame. We sell magazines separately if you need them.

Basic Tools
Punch set, hammer, and standard gunsmithing tools. The DD26.2 assembly process is similar to other DDxx.2 frames, with plenty of video tutorials available online.

3D Printed G26 Build Kit FAQ

Is this a complete 3D printed Glock 26 kit?
This kit includes all the metal and internal components needed to complete a DD26.2 3D printed frame. You provide the printed frame (free files available online) and a magazine. Everything else is in the box.
Will G19 or G17 parts work with this kit?
No. The G26 uses a different locking block, different rails, and some different trigger components than the larger Glocks. You can’t scale down G19 parts for a G26 build. This kit includes the correct G26-specific components.
Can I use G19 magazines?
Yes. The G26 takes any double-stack Glock magazine. G19 mags add 5 rounds and extend about half an inch below the grip. G17 mags work too with a longer extension. For flush-fit, use standard G26 10-round magazines.
Where do I get DD26.2 print files?
DEFCAD, Odyssee, The Gatalog, and similar repositories host the files for free. FreeMenDontAsk (FMDA) created the design. Print settings and assembly documentation are included in the download.
How does this compare to building a DD19.2?
The assembly process is very similar since both use the DDxx.2 rail system. The G26 frame is smaller, so it prints a bit faster. Functionally, the main difference is the shorter grip and slide. If you want something more concealable than a G19, the G26 delivers.
Is building a 3D printed ghost gun legal?
Federal law allows individuals to manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. State and local laws vary, and some places restrict or prohibit home-built firearms. Check your local laws before you order.
Can I build this in .40 S&W?
The DD26.2 frame is compatible with both G26 (9mm) and G27 (.40 S&W) slides. The rails and most lower parts work for both calibers. The ejector and slide are caliber-specific. This kit ships with 9mm components.
Is the slide assembled?
The slide ships complete with all internals, barrel, and sights installed. It’s ready to drop onto your completed frame.

Kit Specifications

Caliber: 9mm Luger

Platform: Glock 26 (subcompact double-stack)

Capacity: 10+1 (flush), 15+1 or 17+1 with extended mags

Rails: Stainless steel, DD26.2 pattern

Locking Block: 17-4 SS, three-pin Gen 3 G26

Frame Compatibility: DD26.2 and FMDA remixes

Cross-Caliber: Frame also accepts G27 (.40 S&W) slides

Not Included: Printed frame, magazine

3D Printed G17 Build Kit Overview

The 3D Printed G17 Build Kit includes everything you need to complete your DD17.2 frame. Instead of tracking down parts from five different vendors and hoping they work together, this kit bundles a complete slide assembly, precision rails, locking block, and full lower parts kit in one box.

We put this kit together specifically for the FMDA DD17.2 3D printed Glock 17 frame. Print your frame, open the box, and start building. Every component is matched and tested, so you’re not troubleshooting compatibility issues mid-build.

What’s Included in This 3D Printed Glock 17 Kit

Complete G17 Slide Assembly
Black nitride slide machined from 416 stainless steel and heat treated to 42 HRC. The kit includes an Optimus Series flush cut barrel with polygonal rifling and 1:10 twist, a complete upper parts kit, and polymer sights with a white dot front. H&M Precision handles the nitride finish, which holds up well to holster wear and corrosion.

DD17.2 Rail & Locking Block Kit
Precision-formed stainless steel rails built for the DDxx.2 mounting system. The front rails are the same proven FMDA G17 design that’s been used in thousands of builds. Rear rails use the improved no-screw system that makes DD17.2 assembly easier and the finished frame stronger.

17-4 Stainless Steel Locking Block

G17 Lower Parts Kit
Everything for the frame internals: trigger bar, trigger housing with 9mm ejector already installed, 5.5lb connector, all springs, slide stop, slide lock, three frame pins, and magazine catch. These drop right into a properly printed frame without fitting.

Why Builders Choose This 3D Printed Glock Kit

One Kit, Zero Compatibility Issues
We selected every component to work together out of the box. The slide uses Gen 3 internals that match the lower parts kit. The rails fit the DD17.2 mounting system. You won’t need to dig through forum posts figuring out what works with what.

100% American Made
The slide and barrel are machined from domestic stainless steel and finished by H&M Precision. Rails and locking block come from Wisconsin. This is a domestic-built parts kit, not a box of mystery imports.

Save Money and Time
Bundle pricing beats buying components separately. You get one shipment instead of four, and you’re not waiting on back-ordered parts from different suppliers while your printed frame collects dust.

Proven Design Platform
The DD17.2 is one of the most tested 3D printed pistol designs out there. Thousands of successful builds, solid documentation, and an active community if you have questions. This kit gives you the parts. The design gives you confidence.

What Else You Need for Your 3D Printed G17

DD17.2 Frame (You Print This)
Files are available on DEFCAD. Search for “DD17.2” or “FMDA Glock 17” and you’ll find them. The download includes print settings, assembly instructions, and video walkthroughs. PLA+ works well for most builders. Glass-filled Zytel produces stronger frames if you have experience with engineering filaments.

Magazine

Basic Tools
A punch set, hammer, and sight pusher will get you through the build. Standard stuff you probably already have.

3D Printed G17 Build Kit FAQ

Is this a complete 3D printed Glock kit?
This kit includes all the metal and internal components you need to finish a DD17.2 3D printed Glock 17 frame. You supply the printed frame and a magazine. Everything else is in the box.
Will this work with other 3D printed Glock frames?
The rails are designed specifically for DD17.2 and its remixes, which use the DDxx.2 mounting system. The slide and lower parts kit will work with any Gen 3 Glock 17 pattern frame. If you’re building a different design, make sure to check rail compatibility before ordering.
What about Glock 22 builds in .40 S&W?
The DD17.2 frame accepts both G17 and G22 slides, so you can build in either caliber. This kit ships with a 9mm upper. The rails and lower parts kit work for .40 as well, so you can always swap the slide later if you want a different caliber.
Where do I get DD17.2 print files?
A membership to DEFCAD.
What filament should I use?
PLA+ is the standard recommendation. Print the frame upright with a 0.4mm nozzle, 0.15mm layers, and 100% infill on critical areas. Glass-filled Zytel makes an extremely durable frame if you’re comfortable printing engineering materials. The file package includes detailed settings.
Is building a 3D printed ghost gun legal?
Federal law allows individuals to manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. State and local laws vary though, and some places restrict or prohibit home-built firearms. Check your local laws before you order.
Do I need gunsmithing experience?
Not really. If you can follow instructions and use basic hand tools, you can finish this build. The DD17.2 has plenty of documentation and video tutorials to walk you through it.
Is the slide assembled?
The slide ships with all parts included but not installed. You’ll put the upper parts kit together and mount the sights yourself. It’s straightforward, and there are plenty of guides online if you need them.

Barrel: 416R SS, polygonal rifling, 1:10 twist, flush cut

Rails: Stainless steel, DDxx.2 pattern

Locking Block: 17-4 SS, replaces Glock #1447

Frame Compatibility: DD17.2 and FMDA remixes

Origin: 100% Made in USA

short_description: A fully DIY .380 ACP firearm featuring custom-designed magazines that integrate a feed ramp directly into the magazine itself, enhancing reliability. It is compatible with FRT and includes an optional MG-34 style grip for improved handling.
description:
Decker 380 Build Kit Overview

The Decker 380 is a fully DIY .380 ACP carbine that requires no traditional firearm components. Everything—the bolt, fire control group, and magazines—is either 3D printed or assembled from hardware store materials. If you’ve been looking for an entry point into semi-automatic DIY firearms that doesn’t require tracking down regulated parts or complex machining, the Decker is it.

This complete build kit includes the barrel, firing pin assembly, springs, bolt weights, and all hardware needed to finish your Decker. Print the files, open the kit, and build. No CNC work, no press fitting, no specialized tooling beyond a basic drill and hex keys.

What Makes the Decker 380 Different

Truly DIY Semi-Automatic
Unlike designs built around AR fire control groups or Glock components, the Decker uses a completely DIY bolt and fire control group. The bolt is assembled from printed parts, threaded rod, and bolt weights included in this kit. No hunting for in-spec FCG parts, no worrying about parts kit availability. Everything you need ships in one box.

Innovative Magazine Design
The Decker’s custom magazines integrate the feed ramp directly into the magazine body rather than the receiver. This design choice simplifies the printed receiver while improving feed reliability. Magazine springs are included in the kit—print the bodies and you’re ready to load.

Configuration Flexibility
The Decker can be built as either a sideloader or toploader, and both configurations are fully ambidextrous. Choose the layout that works for your preferences and use case. The file package includes everything needed for either configuration.

Accessible Build Complexity
The Decker was designed to be one of the easiest semi-automatic firearms to build. The metalwork is limited to drilling a few holes in bar stock—work that can be done with an inexpensive drill on a workbench. Compared to builds like the FGC-9 or Shuty, the Decker dramatically reduces the machining barrier to entry.

FRT Compatibility
The DIY fire control group can be configured for semi-automatic only or semi/FRT operation. The design accommodates both trigger configurations using the same printed components with minor assembly differences.

What’s in the Decker 380 Build Kit

Core Components
The kit includes a .380 Auto barrel, firing pin tube, firing pin, guide rod, recoil spring, trigger spring, safety detent spring, and two magazine springs. These are the functional components that make your Decker run.

Assembly Hardware
Two M5x380 threaded rods and one M5x240 threaded rod form the bolt assembly backbone. Two bolt weights provide the mass needed for reliable cycling. Twenty M5x25 socket head screws handle receiver assembly. A hex key is all you need for final assembly and field stripping.

Decker 380 Build Kit FAQ

Is the Decker 380 Build Kit a complete firearm?
No. The Decker 380 Build Kit contains hardware, barrel, and spring components only. You must 3D print the receiver, bolt components, fire control group, grip, stock, and magazines separately using files from DEFCAD.
Where do I get the Decker 380 print files?
The Decker 380 files are available from DEFCAD. They were released in November 2024. We do not distribute print files directly.
What printer do I need to build the Decker 380?
Any standard FDM printer with sufficient build volume will work. The Decker was designed for accessibility and prints on consumer-grade machines. Check the file documentation for specific print orientation and settings recommendations.
What tools are required to build the Decker 380?
Basic tools only: an electric drill for hole work in the bolt assembly, hex keys for socket head screws (included use), and standard workshop items. No CNC, no lathe, no mill, no press fitting required.
Can I use a different barrel with the Decker 380?
Yes. The Decker supports multiple barrel options including barrel liners, ECM barrels, and Bersa .380 barrels. This kit includes a .380 Auto barrel, but the design accommodates alternatives if you prefer a different sourcing method.
What is the magazine capacity?
The Decker uses custom printed magazines with an integrated feed ramp. Standard capacity is approximately 20 rounds depending on configuration. Two magazine springs are included in this kit.
Is the Decker 380 legal to build?
Under federal law, individuals may manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. However, state and local laws vary significantly. Some jurisdictions prohibit home-built firearms or have specific restrictions on magazine capacity or firearm configurations. It is your responsibility to verify the laws in your area before ordering.
Can I sell a Decker 380 that I build?
Manufacturing firearms with the intent to sell requires a Federal Firearms License. Building for personal use is legal federally; building for sale is a licensed activity. This kit is intended for personal use only.

Legal Compliance

The Decker 380 is designed for legal home manufacture under federal law. Key compliance considerations:

Rifled Barrel: This kit includes a rifled .380 Auto barrel. Using a rifled barrel is required for legal compliance—smoothbore barrels may classify the firearm differently under the NFA.

Overall Length: The Decker is designed as a carbine platform. Ensure your completed build meets minimum overall length requirements (16″ barrel and 26″ OAL for rifle classification, or comply with pistol/SBR regulations as applicable).

State Laws Vary: Some states prohibit home-manufactured firearms, restrict magazine capacity, or have other regulations that may affect the legality of building or possessing a Decker 380. Know your local laws before ordering.

name: Longshot Build Kit
