description:
Longshot Build Kit Overview

The Longshot Build Kit is the extended-barrel variant of the Harlot platform. Same proven single-shot, break-action .22LR design. Same fire control group. Just stretched to a 3″ barrel for improved accuracy and a sleeker profile. If you’ve built a Harlot before, you already know the platform. If this is your first 3D printed firearm, the Longshot Build Kit gives you everything you need to get started.

The Longshot Build Kit includes the complete hardware package: 3″ rifled steel barrel liner (pre-chambered), M3 hardware, hammer spring, latch spring, ejector rod, and firing pin screw. Download the STL files from DEFCAD, print your frame and components in PLA+, and assemble. No machining required.

Where the standard Harlot uses a 1.5″ or 2″ barrel, the Longshot Build Kit stretches that to 3 inches for better velocity and tighter groups at distance. Multiple barrel configurations are available in the file package, including options for optics mounting (RMR, Docter, Shield, C-More, Glock MOS) and Picatinny rails (Short 1913, Long 1913). Same Harlot reliability, more flexibility for precision-minded builds.

What’s Included in the Longshot Build Kit

3″ Rifled Barrel Liner (Pre-Chambered)
Steel .22LR barrel liner, 3 inches long, already chambered and ready to install. No drilling or reaming required. Epoxy into your printed barrel shroud and you’re done.

M3 Hardware Set
Button head hex drive screws (M3 x 20), steel hex nuts, and extras. Everything you need to assemble the frame, secure the barrel latch, and complete the build.

Firing Pin Screw
M3 x 20mm screw, chisel-tipped. Pre-shaped and ready to install.

Springs
Hammer spring (compression) and latch spring included. Cut to length per the assembly drawing if needed.

Ejector Rod
3 x 63mm acetal rod for case ejection. Slides through the breech block to push spent casings out of the chamber.

What Makes the Longshot Build Kit Different

3″ Barrel for Improved Accuracy
The Longshot Build Kit doubles the barrel length compared to the original Harlot. More barrel means better velocity, more consistent ballistics, and tighter groups. The design notes “+5 accuracy” over shorter variants, and builders report noticeably improved performance at 25+ yards.

8 Barrel Configurations
The Longshot Build Kit file package includes eight barrel options: Clean (iron sights only), Short 1913 rail, Long 1913 rail, RMR Cut, Glock MOS, C-More Cut, Docter Cut, and Shield Cut. Mount a red dot, add a rail for accessories, or keep it simple. Your choice.

Cross-Compatible with Harlets Family
The Longshot Build Kit uses the same grip spacers and side panels as the Harlot V2, Quiet Girl, Shizukana, and Artillery Boi. If you’ve already printed custom stippled panels or a UFA-compliant grip spacer for another Harlet, they’ll work here too.

576 Possible Configurations
Between barrel options (8), breech options (2), trigger options (2), hammer options (2), and clipazine/brace options (9), the Longshot Build Kit supports 576 unique configurations. Start with the default build, then customize as you learn the platform.

Longshot Build Kit FAQ

What is the Longshot Build Kit?
The Longshot Build Kit is a hardware package for building the Longshot, a 3″ barrel variant of the Harlot 3D printed pistol. It’s a single-shot, break-action .22LR derringer. The kit includes all metal components: pre-chambered barrel liner, M3 hardware, springs, ejector rod, and firing pin screw. You provide the 3D printed parts (STL files available from DEFCAD).
What’s the difference between the Longshot Build Kit and the standard Harlot?
Barrel length. The original Harlot and Harlot V2 use 1.5″ barrels. The Harlet (V3) uses a 2″ barrel. The Longshot Build Kit uses a 3″ barrel for improved accuracy and velocity. The fire control group, latch mechanism, and general assembly are the same. Side panels and grip spacers are interchangeable between models.
What do I need to complete a Longshot Build Kit?
A 3D printer capable of printing PLA+ (or nylon/polycarbonate), the Longshot STL files from DEFCAD, basic tools (hex drivers, soldering iron for heat inserts if using optic mounts), and .22LR ammunition for testing. The kit includes all metal hardware.
Is the barrel liner in the Longshot Build Kit already chambered?
Yes. The 3″ rifled barrel liner is pre-chambered for .22LR. No drilling, reaming, or polishing required. Epoxy it into your printed barrel shroud and you’re ready to go.
What barrel options are available for the Longshot Build Kit?
Eight configurations: Clean (iron sights), Short 1913 (Picatinny rail), Long 1913, RMR Cut, Glock MOS, C-More Cut, Docter Cut, and Shield Cut. Optic-cut barrels require M3 heat inserts (not included) for mounting your red dot. All barrel STLs are in the Longshot file package.
How accurate is the Longshot Build Kit compared to shorter Harlots?
The 3″ barrel provides noticeably better accuracy than 1.5″ or 2″ variants. The design documentation notes “+5 accuracy” over the standard Harlot. Longer barrel means better velocity and more consistent point of impact. Add a red dot using one of the optic-cut barrel options for even better precision.
What filament should I use for the Longshot Build Kit?
PLA+ is the tested and recommended material. Nylon and polycarbonate have also seen functional success. The breech block must be printed at 6 walls/top/bottom with 99% infill and 3X infill line multiplier. Print the latch and hammer with the same settings. Other parts can use 15%+ infill.
Is the Longshot Build Kit legal?
Under federal law, building a firearm for personal use is legal in most circumstances. The barrel liner must be rifled (not smoothbore) to avoid AOW classification. UFA-compliant grip spacers are included in the file package for installing 3.7oz of metal mass if required in your jurisdiction. State and local laws vary significantly. It is your responsibility to verify the laws in your area before building.

Specifications & Legal

Platform: Longshot (Harlets Family)

Caliber: .22LR

Action: Single-shot, break-action

Barrel Length: 3″ (rifled steel liner, pre-chambered)

Barrel Options: 8 configurations (Clean, Short 1913, Long 1913, RMR, Glock MOS, C-More, Docter, Shield)

Kit Includes: 3″ barrel liner, M3 hardware, firing pin screw, hammer spring, latch spring, ejector rod

You Provide: 3D printed parts (STL files from DEFCAD), epoxy, basic tools, ammunition

Tested Durability: 400+ rounds

Print Material: PLA+ recommended (nylon/PC also functional)

Legal Notes: Rifled barrel required (smoothbore may be AOW). UFA grip spacers included in files for 3.7oz metal requirement. Verify state and local laws before building.

Brawler Build Kit Overview

The Brawler takes the proven Harlot platform and wraps it in a knuckle duster frame that’s equal parts functional firearm and conversation piece. This single-shot .22LR break-action derringer includes the same reliable operation as the original Harlot in a grip style that’s genuinely unique in the 3D printed firearms space.

This build kit includes the .22LR rifled barrel liner, springs, all mounting hardware. The Brawler shares the same fire control group and breech design as other Harlot variants—proven components with thousands of successful builds. Print the frame, assemble the kit, and you’ve got a working .22LR pistol that looks like nothing else on the range.

What Makes the Brawler Different

Distinctive Knuckle Duster Design
The Brawler’s four-finger grip frame isn’t just for aesthetics—it provides a secure, natural hold that keeps the pistol locked in your hand during firing. The grip geometry distributes recoil across your knuckles rather than your palm, creating a different shooting experience than traditional derringer designs.

Proven Harlot Internals
Under the unique exterior, the Brawler uses the same fire control group, breech design, and barrel system as other Harlot variants. This isn’t an experimental platform—it’s a proven .22LR action in a new package. The break-action design is simple, reliable, and easy to understand.

Beginner-Friendly Assembly
Like all Harlots, the Brawler was designed for accessibility. If you can operate a 3D printer and turn a screwdriver, you can build this pistol. No press-fitting, no drilling beyond basic deburring, no machining. The assembly process follows the same steps as the original Harlot—video tutorials apply directly.

BrassTax Option Included
The designs are identical—BrassTax simply uses brass material for the frame instead of printed plastic. Brass stock is not included in the kit, but the files are there if you want to machine your own metal version.

What’s in the Brawler Build Kit

Components
.22LR rifled barrel liner (requires chambering), hammer spring, and all necessary springs for the fire control group. These are the same proven components used across the Harlot family.

Hardware
M3 bolts in required lengths, M3 nuts, and hex key for assembly. Everything needed to complete the build except the UFA-required metal weight.

Brawler Build Kit FAQ

Is the Brawler Build Kit a complete firearm?
No. The Brawler Build Kit contains hardware and barrel components only. You must 3D print the Brawler frame and other structural components separately using the files found at DEFCAD.
What printer do I need to build the Brawler?
Any standard FDM printer with a typical build volume will work. The Brawler was designed to print on entry-level machines without specialized modifications. PLA+ is the tested and recommended material.
How is the Brawler different from other Harlots?
The Brawler uses the same fire control group and barrel system as other Harlot variants but features a distinctive knuckle duster grip frame. Internally, it operates identically to the standard Harlot—the difference is entirely in the grip and frame design.
What is BrassTax?
BrassTax is the brass-framed version of the Brawler. The Brawler kit does not include brass material—if you want to build a BrassTax, you’ll need to source and machine your own brass stock.
Does the barrel liner come chambered?
No. The barrel liner must be chambered with a #1 wire gauge drill bit and carefully deburred with a small round file or countersink tool before installation. Watch the Harlot assembly tutorial video for detailed instructions on this process.
What tools do I need to complete the build?
Hex driver for M3 screws, #1 wire gauge drill bit for chambering the liner, small round file or countersink for deburring, epoxy for securing the barrel liner, and wire cutters to trim springs to length. A soldering iron is helpful for installing heat-set inserts.
How does the half-cock safety work?
The Brawler features a half-cock position on the hammer. If you store the pistol with a round chambered, always keep the hammer at half-cock. This is a passive safety feature—not a recommendation to store loaded firearms.
Is the Brawler legal to build?
Under federal law, individuals may manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. However, state and local laws vary significantly. Some jurisdictions prohibit home-built firearms entirely. It is your responsibility to verify the laws in your area before ordering.
Can I sell a Brawler I build?
Manufacturing firearms with the intent to sell requires a Federal Firearms License. Building for personal use is legal federally; building for sale is a licensed activity. This kit is intended for personal use only.

Legal Compliance

The Brawler is designed for legal home manufacture under federal law. Key compliance features:

Rifled Barrel: Kit includes a rifled .22LR barrel liner. Using a smoothbore tube may classify the firearm as an AOW under the NFA. Always use the rifled liner provided.

Metal Weight Requirement: Under the 1988 Undetectable Firearms Act, this build requires 3.7oz of stainless steel to be placed into the printed spacer before assembly. Metal weight is not included in this kit—builders are responsible for sourcing and installing the required weight.

State Laws Vary: Some states prohibit home-manufactured firearms. Know your local laws before ordering.

description:
Harlot [3.0] Overview

The Harlot [3.0] is the definitive version of the most popular 3D printed handgun ever released. The Harlot has been through multiple iterations over the years. Version 3.0 (also known as the “Harlet”) combines all the best upgrades into one package: improved ergonomics, better sights, a smoother trigger, and an easier-to-use barrel latch.

This is still a single-shot, break-action .22LR derringer at heart. But everything that made the original Harlot good has been made better. If you’ve built a V1 or V2, the Harlot [3.0] is a noticeable step up. If this is your first 3D printed firearm, you’re starting with the best version.

The Harlot [3.0] Build Kit includes every non-printed component you need: a pre-chambered 2″ rifled barrel liner, all hardware with extras, springs. Print the files, open the kit, assemble.

What’s New in Harlot [3.0]

Larger Frame, Better Grip
The Harlot [3.0] features an enlarged frame compared to V1 and V2. More material means a better grip, improved control during firing, and a more comfortable shooting experience. The derringer is still compact, but now it actually fits your hand.

Improved Barrel Latch
Breaking open the action on earlier Harlots could be finicky. The V3 barrel latch mechanism has been completely redesigned for smoother, more reliable operation. Open, load, close, fire. No fighting with the mechanism.

Better Trigger and Sights
The Harlot [3.0] includes an improved trigger design for a cleaner break. Sights have also been refined for easier target acquisition. Small changes that make a noticeable difference at the range.

Longer Barrel
V3 uses a 2″ barrel liner (up from the original 37mm). The extra length improves accuracy and provides a more complete powder burn, resulting in better velocity from the .22LR cartridge.

Harlot [3.0] FAQ

Is the Harlot [3.0] Build Kit a complete firearm?
No. The Harlot [3.0] Build Kit contains hardware, springs, and barrel components only. You must 3D print the frame, grip, and other structural components separately using files from DEFCAD.
Where do I get the Harlot [3.0] print files?
The Harlot [3.0] (Harlet) STL files are available from DEFCAD. We do not distribute the print files directly. Search for “Harlet V3” to find the correct version.
What printer do I need to build the Harlot [3.0]?
Any standard FDM printer with a typical build volume will work. The Harlot [3.0] was designed to print on entry-level machines without specialized modifications. PLA or PLA+ filament is recommended (Esun PLA+ is popular in the community).
What are the recommended print settings for the Harlot [3.0]?
Print the breech block at 99% infill. All other parts should use at least 6 walls, 6 top/bottom layers, and 15% infill with a 3X line multiplier. Do not use supports or brims. Consult the README included with the print files for complete settings.
Is the Harlot [3.0] legal to build?
Under federal law, individuals may manufacture firearms for personal use without a license. However, state and local laws vary significantly. Some jurisdictions prohibit home-built firearms entirely. It is your responsibility to verify the laws in your area before ordering.
What is the UFA grip weight option?
Federal law (the Undetectable Firearms Act) requires handguns to contain a minimum of 3.7oz of metal. The optional UFA grip weight is designed to meet this requirement. If you prefer to add your own metal weight, select the option without the grip weight.
Can I sell a Harlot [3.0] I build?
Manufacturing firearms with the intent to sell requires an FFL. Building for personal use is legal federally; building for sale is a licensed activity. This kit is intended for personal use only.

Legal Compliance

The Harlot [3.0] is designed for legal home manufacture under federal law. Key compliance features:

Rifled Barrel: Kit includes a rifled .22 barrel liner. Using a smoothbore tube may classify the firearm as an AOW under the NFA. Always use the rifled liner provided.

Metal Weight Requirement: Federal law (UFA) requires handguns to contain a minimum of 3.7oz of metal. The optional UFA grip weight is available to meet this requirement. Builders are responsible for ensuring compliance.

State Laws Vary: Some states prohibit home-manufactured firearms. Know your local laws before ordering the Harlot [3.0] Build Kit.
